section: Right to Constitutional Remedies - Article 32; the five writs and their scope
subsections: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie
Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure
Guardian of Fundamental Rights; number of writs

accepted.s: Which of the following is guaranteed as a Fundamental Right under Article 32(1) of the Constitution of India?
o: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for enforcement of Fundamental Rights
The right to appeal against every decision of a High Court
The right to seek an advisory opinion from the Supreme Court on every constitutional matter
The right to move any subordinate court for enforcement of statutory rights
accepted.x: Article 32(1) guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise constitutional guarantee rather than a broader appellate or advisory power.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Under Article 32(2) of the Constitution, the Supreme Court may issue which of the following for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
1. Directions
2. Orders
3. Writs
4. Advisory opinions only
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: Article 32(2) empowers the Supreme Court to issue directions, orders and writs, including the five named writs. Advisory opinions are not included in this provision.
accepted.tq: Separate the enforcement remedies under Article 32 from the Supreme Court’s advisory jurisdiction.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 32(3) of the Constitution:
1. Parliament may empower any other court to exercise some of the powers of the Supreme Court under Article 32.
2. Parliament has so far enacted a law empowering subordinate courts to issue writs under Article 32.
3. High Courts issue writs under Article 226.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Article 32(3) permits Parliament to empower other courts, but no such law has been made so far. High Courts issue writs under Article 226.
accepted.tq: Watch for the trap that changes a constitutional enabling provision into an enacted law.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Article 32(4) of the Constitution of India?
o: The right under Article 32 is available only during a National Emergency
The right under Article 32 shall not be suspended except as otherwise provided by the Constitution
The right under Article 32 may be suspended by an ordinary law of Parliament
The right under Article 32 can never be suspended under any circumstances
accepted.x: Article 32(4) provides that the right guaranteed by Article 32 shall not be suspended except as otherwise provided by the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Distinguish constitutional limitation from absolute or ordinary-legislative restrictions.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements best expresses the constitutional position of Article 32?
o: It is a statutory remedy created by Parliament and may be withdrawn by Parliament
It can be completely repealed by a constitutional amendment because it is procedural
It forms part of the basic structure and cannot be abridged even by a constitutional amendment
It applies only to legal rights created by ordinary legislation
accepted.x: Article 32 is part of the basic structure of the Constitution. Its essential guarantee cannot be abridged even through a constitutional amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the basic-structure doctrine to reject options treating a Fundamental Right as an ordinary statutory remedy.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is best described as
o: original and exclusive
advisory but not original
original but not exclusive
appellate and exclusive
accepted.x: Article 32 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction to enforce Fundamental Rights, but this jurisdiction is not exclusive because High Courts also exercise writ jurisdiction under Article 226.
accepted.tq: Split the paired descriptions—original and exclusive—instead of assuming that direct jurisdiction is exclusive.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person seeks enforcement of a right created only by an ordinary statute, without alleging violation of a Fundamental Right. Which of the following is correct?
o: Article 32 is not the appropriate remedy because it enforces only Fundamental Rights
Article 32 automatically converts the statutory right into a Fundamental Right
The person can directly invoke Article 32 as a matter of right
Article 32 can be invoked only if the President permits it
accepted.x: Article 32 is confined to enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Statutory rights and other non-Fundamental constitutional rights cannot ordinarily be enforced under Article 32.
accepted.tq: Apply the scope of the remedy to distinguish Fundamental Rights from statutory rights.
accepted.sec: Article 32 - right to move SC directly, "heart and soul", basic structure  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the writ of Prohibition?
o: Issued against a private person to compel performance of a contract
Issued by a higher court to stop a lower judicial or quasi-judicial body from exceeding its jurisdiction
Issued to test the legality of a person’s claim to a public office
Issued to release a person from every form of lawful detention
accepted.x: Prohibition is issued by a higher court to prevent a lower court or tribunal with judicial or quasi-judicial functions from exceeding its jurisdiction.
accepted.tq: Match the writ with the body against which it operates and the stage at which it acts.
accepted.sec: Writ → literal meaning and purpose  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A writ of Prohibition does NOT ordinarily lie against which of the following?
o: A judicial body
A quasi-judicial tribunal
An administrative authority acting administratively
A lower court exceeding its jurisdiction
accepted.x: Prohibition lies against judicial and quasi-judicial bodies, but not against administrative authorities acting in an administrative capacity. It also does not lie against legislative bodies or private persons.
accepted.tq: Find the body outside the judicial or quasi-judicial field.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Certiorari is correct?
o: It is confined exclusively to private disputes between individuals
It can be issued only before a lower court begins proceedings
It may transfer a case or quash an order of a lower court or authority
It is available only against a legislative body
accepted.x: Certiorari may be used to transfer a case from, or quash an order of, a lower court or authority. It operates against judicial, quasi-judicial and certain administrative bodies affecting rights.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the corrective function of Certiorari from the preventive function of Prohibition.
accepted.sec: Writ → literal meaning and purpose  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Since 1991, the writ of Certiorari may also lie against
o: Certain administrative bodies when their actions affect rights
All legislative bodies without exception
Every private individual
The President and Governor for their official acts
accepted.x: The scope of Certiorari has been extended to certain administrative bodies whose decisions affect rights. It does not ordinarily lie against private persons or legislative bodies.
accepted.tq: Use the date-linked expansion of jurisdiction to identify the precise category added.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mandamus does NOT ordinarily lie against which of the following?
o: The President or Governor for official acts
An inferior court failing to perform a public legal duty
A public corporation
A public official
accepted.x: Mandamus may lie against public officials, public corporations, inferior courts, tribunals and government authorities, but not against the President or Governor for their official acts. Article 361 protects them from being answerable to any court for official acts.
accepted.tq: Apply the question ‘who would perform this public duty?’ and remember the constitutional protection of the President and Governors.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a limitation on the issue of Mandamus?
o: It may be issued only by a subordinate civil court
It may be issued against a private individual for any personal dispute
It is not issued to enforce a merely discretionary duty or a private contractual obligation
It may be issued to enforce every private contractual obligation
accepted.x: Mandamus enforces a public legal duty. It does not ordinarily lie for a merely discretionary duty, a private contractual obligation, non-statutory instructions or against private persons.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a public legal duty from a private or discretionary obligation.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Habeas Corpus, consider the following statements:
1. It may be directed against public authorities.
2. It may also be directed against a private individual who unlawfully detains another person.
3. It necessarily results in release even when the detention is lawful.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Habeas Corpus may be issued against public authorities and private individuals for unlawful detention. It does not require release where the detention is lawful.
accepted.tq: Separate the persons against whom the writ lies from the condition that makes detention unlawful.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Habeas Corpus does NOT ordinarily lie in respect of
o: Illegal detention by a private individual
Illegal detention by a public authority
Lawful detention or detention pursuant to a valid court order
A demand to produce a detained person before the court
accepted.x: Habeas Corpus is a remedy against unlawful detention. It does not lie against lawful detention, contempt of court or legislature, or detention outside the jurisdiction of the court.
accepted.tq: Look for the legality of detention before deciding whether Habeas Corpus is available.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A person challenges the occupation of a substantive public office created by the Constitution. Who may ordinarily seek a writ of Quo Warranto?
o: Any interested person, even if not personally aggrieved
Only a member of the concerned legislature
Only the person personally aggrieved by the appointment
Only the Attorney-General of India
accepted.x: Quo Warranto may be sought by any interested person; personal aggrievement is not an essential requirement. The writ tests the legality of a person’s claim to a substantive public office.
accepted.tq: Use the standing rule to avoid importing the personal-aggrievement requirement of private litigation.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Quo Warranto does NOT ordinarily lie in relation to
o: An unlawful claim to a public office
A private office or a merely ministerial office
A substantive office created by the Constitution
A substantive office created by statute
accepted.x: Quo Warranto examines the legality of a claim to a substantive public office created by the Constitution or a statute. It does not lie against a private or merely ministerial office.
accepted.tq: First identify whether the office is substantive and public before applying Quo Warranto.
accepted.sec: Writ → against whom it lies and does not lie  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The writ jurisdiction of Indian constitutional courts is historically derived from the
o: English law of prerogative writs issued in the name of the King
Roman law of civil obligations
United States doctrine of judicial review alone
French system of administrative courts
accepted.x: The writs were borrowed from English law, where they were known as prerogative writs of the King, regarded as the fountain of justice.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional borrowing by linking the writs with their historical institutional source.
accepted.sec: Writ → literal meaning and purpose  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding writ jurisdiction in India is correct?
1. Before 1950, the High Courts of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras could issue writs.
2. Article 226 now empowers all High Courts to issue writs.
3. Article 226 confines High Court writ jurisdiction exclusively to Fundamental Rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Before 1950, the Calcutta, Bombay and Madras High Courts had writ jurisdiction. Article 226 now empowers all High Courts, and their jurisdiction extends beyond Fundamental Rights to other purposes as well.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word ‘exclusively’ by comparing the wider scope of Article 226 with Article 32.
accepted.sec: Guardian of Fundamental Rights; number of writs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the institutional position regarding protection of Fundamental Rights?
o: Only Parliament is the protector and guarantor of Fundamental Rights
The President is the final guardian of Fundamental Rights
Only the Supreme Court can protect Fundamental Rights
The Supreme Court is the protector and guarantor of Fundamental Rights, while High Courts also share this role under Article 226
accepted.x: The judiciary, particularly the Supreme Court, is the protector and guarantor of Fundamental Rights. High Courts also exercise this role through their jurisdiction under Article 226.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the principal constitutional guardian from the authorities that make or implement laws.
accepted.sec: Guardian of Fundamental Rights; number of writs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: How many writs are specifically recognised for enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 32(2)?
o: Three
Six
Four
Five
accepted.x: Article 32(2) refers to five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto.
accepted.tq: Count the constitutionally named writs rather than adding other judicial remedies.
accepted.sec: Guardian of Fundamental Rights; number of writs  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which writ is traditionally regarded as the bulwark of individual liberty?
o: Quo Warranto
Prohibition
Habeas Corpus
Mandamus
accepted.x: Habeas Corpus is regarded as the bulwark of individual liberty because it provides a prompt judicial remedy against unlawful detention.
accepted.tq: Associate the liberty-protection function with the writ directed against unlawful detention.
accepted.sec: Guardian of Fundamental Rights; number of writs  [APPSC]
